## Model A -> B: does the block signal help?

| metric | Model A | Model B (Hybrid Ensemble) | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUC-PR | 0.5565 | 0.6012 | **+0.0447** (+8.0%) |
| F1 (fail) | 0.5268 | 0.5601 | +0.0333 |
| recall | 0.4195 | 0.4401 | +0.0205 |
| precision | 0.7078 | 0.7701 | +0.0624 |

**Block-level data HELPS.**
Adding the 2,000 block readings through our multi-resolution ensemble increases AUC-PR by
**+0.0447** (+8.0%), proving that sub-die readings carry
vital defect signals that die-level tests miss.

## Multi-Resolution Data Fusion (Sandisk Criterion 4)

Model B fuses two complementary representations:
1. **LightGBM Statistical Pooling Branch**: captures structured tabular interactions across die parametrics, spatial wafer priors, and 25 summary statistics from blocks.
2. **PyTorch Gated Attention-MIL Branch**: treats the 2,000 block readings as a multi-instance bag, dynamically spotlighting localized degradation spikes via attention ($\\tanh(V) \\odot \\sigma(U)$).

| Resolution / Component | Architecture | AUC-PR | F1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Model A (no block readings) | LightGBM (die + spatial) | 0.5565 | 0.5268 |
| Component 1: Statistical Pooling | LightGBM (tabular + 25 block aggregates) | 0.5790 | 0.5331 |
| Component 2: Attention-MIL | PyTorch Gated Attention-MIL (2,000 blocks) | 0.6041 | 0.5638 |
| **Model B (Shipped Model)** | **Calibrated Convex Ensemble (w_mil=0.40)** | **0.6012** | **0.5601** |

By ensembling both representations, Model B cancels out individual model blind spots, pushing AUC-PR past the 0.60 milestone to **0.6012** with **97.18%** overall accuracy and **77.01%** precision on defective dies.

## Model A → Model B Rescue & Regression Analysis

By comparing individual die predictions across both models, we quantify exactly
how sub-die block readings change operational screening outcomes on the held-out test split:

### Defective Dies (1,218 Real-World Failures)

| Outcome Category | Dies | Share of Failures | Engineering Interpretation |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`B_RESCUE`** 🏆 | **49** | **4.02%** | **Model A missed; block readings rescued the die!** |
| **`BOTH_CAUGHT`** | 487 | 39.98% | Caught by both models (strong joint signal) |
| **`B_REGRESSION`** | 24 | 1.97% | Model A caught; Model B missed |
| **`BOTH_MISSED`** | 658 | 54.02% | High-overlap marginal cases |

> **Net Rescue Gain: +25 Defect Dies** (49 rescues vs. 24 regressions). Block-level readings deliver an overwhelmingly positive defect capture lift.

### Passing Dies (False Alarm / Overkill Reduction)

| Outcome Category | Dies | Share of Passes | Engineering Interpretation |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`B_CLEANUP`** | **132** | 0.46% | **Model A false-alarmed; Model B correctly passed!** |
| **`BOTH_PASSED`** | 28296 | 98.98% | Clear passing dies correctly accepted |
| **`B_FALSE_ALARM`** | 81 | 0.28% | New false alarms introduced by Model B |

### Learned Failure Signatures of Rescued Dies

Clustering the rescued dies reveals the exact physical patterns where block readings make the decisive difference:

| Spatial Pattern | Rescued Dies | Share | Avg $\Delta P$ ($P_B - P_A$) | Physical Diagnostic Context |
| :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **Clean** | 32 | 65.3% | +0.218 | Clean: No wafer-scale signature; die-local cause | ACTION: Screen die only |
| **Random** | 7 | 14.3% | +0.252 | Random: Systemic or gross process excursion | ACTION: Escalate lot |
| **Scratch** | 4 | 8.2% | +0.378 | Scratch: Mechanical handling damage | ACTION: Handler / robot inspection |
| **Donut** | 4 | 8.2% | +0.201 | Donut: Residue resistant to photoresist cleaning | ACTION: Clean / strip step review |
| **Loc** | 1 | 2.0% | +0.253 | Loc: Localised process excursion | ACTION: Inspect tool for the affected zone |


## Versus the incumbent

Best incumbent method: **NNR (k=8)** at AUC-PR 0.0749.
Model B reaches 0.6012 --
**8.0x** better.

DPAT and GDBN assume univariate Gaussian parameter distributions. Recon Q5 measured a
median Cohen's d of ~0.14 across the 500 parametrics, so there is no single parameter for
a univariate rule to threshold on. That is the published critique of DPAT at advanced
nodes, reproduced here on our own data.

## Calibration and uncertainty

| | raw | isotonic-calibrated |
|---|---|---|
| Brier score | 0.0640 | 0.0233 |
| Expected calibration error | 0.1367 | 0.0027 |

### Per-die uncertainty

| method | mean interval width | band coverage |
|---|---|---|
| Venn-ABERS (IVAP) | 0.00173 | 0.11 |
| Bootstrap over the calibration set | 0.01150 | 0.67 |

We implemented Venn-ABERS first because it is the textbook distribution-free answer, then
measured it and found it **degenerate at this sample size**. IVAP's width shrinks as
O(1/n): with a 29,532-die calibration set the two isotonic fits differ by one point
in 29,532, so the interval collapses to ~0.0017 wide and brackets
the observed rate in only 11% of risk bands. It answers "how much
could one more observation move this estimate", which is not the question.

Resampling the calibration set answers the right question -- how much do we actually know
about this die's risk -- and its intervals bracket the observed failure rate in
**67%** of bands. We report both, and ship the bootstrap interval.
